title: The completed coefficient map is an isomorphism, without a completeness hypothesis on any module.
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, chosen uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and quotient rings $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_E$ for $m\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of arbitrary schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $\Phi_g(U\xrightarrow{u}X)=(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$ and let $F_g$ be the sectionwise inverse-image functor on ring sheaves, $(F_g\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(\Phi_gU)$ [def-weil-proetale-iso-sectionwise-inverse-image]. Schemes and coefficients may have independent universes $t,u$; take ring sheaves valued in $\operatorname{RingCat}_{\max(u,t+1)}$, using $\operatorname{ULift}^{t+1}A_{E,m}$ for the coefficient rings.

For $W=X,Y$ and $n\in\mathbf N$, let $R_{W,n}$ be the constant commutative ring sheaf with value $\operatorname{ULift}^{t+1}A_{E,n+1}$, regarded as a sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $r_{W,n}:R_{W,n+1}\to R_{W,n}$ for its quotient transition, and put $L_W=\varprojlim_{n\in\mathbf N}R_{W,n}$, with projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Thus $R_{W,\bullet}$ and $L_W$ are precisely `integralCoefficientSheafSystem` and `completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted`.

Let $c_n:F_gR_{Y,n}\to R_{X,n}$ be the canonical comparison fixed by sending each constant section $a$ at $\Phi_gU$ to the constant section $a$ at $U$, as in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (3). Let $q:F_gL_Y\to L_X$ be the limit lift specified by
$$\pi_{X,n}\circ q=c_n\circ F_g(\pi_{Y,n})\qquad(n\in\mathbf N).$$
This is the recorded `inverseImageCompletedCoefficientMap l E g`. Then $q$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. No module or completeness hypothesis on a module is part of this assertion.

proof.text: The site equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] gives the sheafification compatibility isomorphism. Its action on constant sections is the prescribed normalization. Uniqueness therefore identifies its underlying ring-sheaf map with each finite coefficient comparison, proving those comparisons invertible. The naturality square proved in the component-naturality argument assembles these comparisons into a natural transformation of coefficient diagrams. NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app makes it a natural isomorphism.

I read the four steps against every cited statement and against the Lean, read-only: InverseImagePullbackComparison.lean 44-120 and IsoSectionwiseInverseImage.lean 130-215. The statement is true and matches inverseImageCompletedCoefficientMap_isIso exactly: g is any scheme isomorphism, the universes t and u are independent, the exponent is n+1, the map is the limit lift of the constant-section-normalized maps, and nothing is added or dropped. I tested it on g=id, the empty scheme and n=0. The normalization in the statement is necessary, because a constant ring sheaf with value O_E/ϖ^m can have ring maps out of it other than the normalized one (for example Frobenius when E is unramified); the statement has it. One fault, C3/C4, in Step 1. The step cites part (3) of lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image for the invertibility and quotient-naturality of the sectionwise c_n. But that part's statement is about c^g_A for the adjoint inverse image g^{-1}, and part (1) gives the identification with the sectionwise functor F_g only as some unpinned natural isomorphism. The link to the normalized sectionwise map is in that lemma's proof (Steps 5-6) and its Lean, not its statement. FIX: Step 1 now proves existence, uniqueness, inverse and naturality of c_n directly. It uses part (1) of the lemma (Φ_g and Φ_h quasi-inverse and covering-preserving), F_g and F_h from def-weil-proetale-iso-sectionwise-inverse-image (identities on constant presheaves), and the universal property of sheafification from def-weil-pbc-sheafification and def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf. Both nodes are added to uses and proof_deps. Steps 2-4 (the coordinate formula for q, the coordinatewise inverse with its transition and restriction squares, and the identities) are correct and unchanged. I removed the declared tool use: the unit sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation cites sk-def-sf-admissible, the lemma's own unit, so the citation is already on route and no tool use is accepted. Duplicate search over the DAG: the limit-scalar-chain node assumes the completed isomorphisms, and the derived-pullback-reduction-tower node is about adjoint g^{-1}, so neither is a duplicate. The unsplit provisional component-naturality node is a sibling that Step 1 now proves inline.
